name: Walking Lunge
description: The walking lunge is a unilateral lower body exercise that trains the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings in a dynamic stepping pattern. By stepping forward and alternating legs, it trains single-leg strength and balance while requiring the muscles of the hip and knee to work through full range of motion.

execution.starting_position: Stand tall with feet together and core braced. If using dumbbells, hold one in each hand at the sides.
execution.setup_instructions: Ensure adequate floor space to walk several meters. Bodyweight is recommended before adding load.
steps: Step forward with one leg, landing heel first.
Lower the rear knee toward the floor until the front thigh is roughly parallel to the floor.
Drive through the front heel to bring the rear foot forward and step into the next lunge on the other leg.
Continue alternating legs for the prescribed distance or rep count.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you push off the front foot. Inhale as you step forward.
common_mistakes: Front knee caving inward — push the knee out in line with the toes
Leaning excessively forward with the torso
Taking too short a stride, forcing the knee too far over the toes
safety_considerations: If knee pain is present, reduce range of motion or switch to a split squat
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Front thigh parallel to floor or lower. Rear knee just above or touching the floor.
coaching_cues: Long stride — your shin on the front leg should be close to vertical
Tall torso throughout — do not let your upper body collapse forward
